neighbours.label: 'out' after a form of the verb run, and the 'of' that follows, whether the running out is literal or depletion; also weakly 'low' or 'short' after run
fire: I am worried that the shelter will run out of blankets this week.
The bakery ran out of flour before the morning rush was over.
Our team is running out of ideas for the spring campaign.
The children ran out onto the beach the moment the car stopped.
My passport runs out in about two months, so I must renew it.
The farm's water ran low during the driest part of the summer.
He had run out of patience long before the meeting ended.
They are running short of nurses at the county hospital.
quiet: I am worried that the shelter will give away its blankets this week.
The bakery sold out of bread before the morning rush was over.
Our team is coming up with ideas for the spring campaign.
The children walked out onto the beach the moment the car stopped.
My passport expires in about two months, so I must renew it.
The farm's water ran clear during the driest part of the summer.
He had taken out a pen long before the meeting ended.
They are running a clinic for nurses at the county hospital.

notes: Probes: 'ran out the door' fires as well as 'ran out of milk', so the verb phrase matters, not depletion. 'sold out of', 'walked out of', 'ran away' stay quiet. 'ran low' and 'running short' fire at about 0.5.
